questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A geostationary satellite orbits at an altitude of about 35,786 km above the equator.
2. A geostationary orbit can have any inclination to the equatorial plane.
3. A geostationary satellite appears fixed in the sky because its orbital period equals the Earth's rotation period and it moves in the same direction as the Earth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: To hover over one spot the satellite must be in the equatorial plane (zero inclination) with a 24-hour period. An inclined geosynchronous orbit makes the satellite swing north and south of the equator.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Sun-synchronous orbit is a near-polar orbit.
2. A satellite in Sun-synchronous orbit passes over a given place at the same local solar time every day.
3. Sun-synchronous satellites are usually placed at about 36,000 km above the Earth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Such satellites orbit at roughly 600-800 km, and the orbital plane precesses with the Sun, so lighting conditions remain the same for repeat images. The 36,000 km altitude is that of geostationary satellites.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Passive remote sensing sensors emit their own radiation to illuminate the target.
2. Synthetic Aperture Radar is an active microwave sensor.
3. Microwave radar imaging can acquire images through cloud cover and at night.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Passive sensors only record reflected sunlight or emitted heat. SAR sends out its own microwaves, so it works by day or night and microwaves pass through clouds, making it valuable for floods and monsoon-time monitoring.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Spatial resolution of a sensor refers to the time gap between two successive passes over the same area.
2. Temporal resolution refers to the number of spectral bands recorded by a sensor.
3. Hyperspectral sensors record data in a large number of narrow, contiguous spectral bands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Spatial resolution is the smallest feature that can be distinguished on the ground; temporal resolution is the revisit time. The statements swap the two, while hyperspectral imaging with hundreds of narrow bands is correctly described.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. PSLV is a four-stage launch vehicle that uses solid and liquid propulsion stages alternately.
2. PSLV uses a cryogenic upper stage.
3. In February 2017, a single PSLV mission placed 104 satellites in orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PSLV stages are solid, liquid, solid, liquid. The cryogenic upper stage belongs to GSLV and LVM3, and PSLV-C37 carried 104 satellites including Cartosat-2 series satellite.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) is a two-stage vehicle without any cryogenic stage.
2. Cryogenic stages use liquid hydrogen as fuel and liquid oxygen as oxidiser.
3. Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LVM3 has two solid strap-on boosters, a liquid core stage and a cryogenic upper stage (C25), which gives it its capacity to put about 4 tonnes into geosynchronous transfer orbit. The same vehicle carried Chandrayaan-3 in July 2023.
questions.h: Cryogenic: LH2 at -253 C, LOX at -183 C.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandrayaan-1 was launched in 2019.
2. The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-2 made a successful soft landing on the Moon.
3. The lander of Chandrayaan-3 touched down near the south polar region of the Moon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-1 was launched in 2008 and Vikram of Chandrayaan-2 lost contact and crashed during the final descent in 2019. Chandrayaan-3 landed in August 2023 near the lunar south pole, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.
questions.h: Chandrayaan-3: 4th country to land, 1st near the south pole.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mars Orbiter Mission was launched by GSLV.
2. India became the first Asian nation to reach the Martian orbit.
3. India became the first country to reach the Mars orbit in its maiden attempt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MOM was launched by PSLV-C25 in November 2013 and entered Mars orbit in September 2014. Earlier Asian attempts by Japan and China had failed to reach Mars orbit, while some other countries took more than one attempt.
questions.h: MOM: first attempt, first in Asia.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. NavIC provides global navigation coverage.
2. NavIC primarily covers India and a region extending about 1,500 km around it.
3. The NavIC constellation consists of seven satellites, all in geostationary orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NavIC (formerly IRNSS) is a regional system. Its seven satellites are three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbits.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Outer Space Treaty prohibits the placing of nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction in orbit around the Earth.
2. The Outer Space Treaty came into force in 1967.
3. The Outer Space Treaty allows a State to claim sovereignty over the Moon if it lands there first.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The treaty bans national appropriation of the Moon and other celestial bodies by claim of sovereignty, use or occupation, and bars WMD in orbit.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. IN-SPACe is the commercial arm of ISRO.
2. NewSpace India Limited is a public sector company under the Department of Space.
3. Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S, launched in 2022, was the first privately developed rocket launched from India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NSIL is the commercial arm of ISRO, while IN-SPACe is a separate authorisation and promotion body for private players. Vikram-S was a sub-orbital flight from Sriharikota.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Aditya-L1 is India's first space-based observatory for studying the Sun.
2. At the Sun-Earth L1 point the gravitational pulls of the Sun and the Earth cancel exactly, so a spacecraft needs no propulsion to stay there.
3. The James Webb Space Telescope is also located at the Sun-Earth L1 point.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: L1 is an unstable balance point, so periodic station-keeping burns are needed, and Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit around it. The James Webb Space Telescope is at the L2 point on the far side of the Earth.
questions.h: JWST is L2, Aditya is L1.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gaganyaan plans to carry a crew of three to an orbit of about 400 km for up to three days.
2. Vyommitra is a female humanoid robot used in the uncrewed test flights.
3. Gaganyaan's crew module is planned to be launched by PSLV.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The mission uses a human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) because the heavier crew module is beyond PSLV's capacity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A rocket works on the principle of Newton's third law of motion.
2. A rocket can function in the vacuum of space.
3. A rocket needs the atmosphere to push against to move forward.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rockets expel exhaust at high speed and are pushed the other way; no air is required, and in fact there is less drag in space. Rockets carry their own oxidiser.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. INSAT is a multipurpose system used for telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology and search and rescue.
2. INSAT satellites are placed in low Earth orbit.
3. Kalpana-1 was India's first dedicated meteorological satellite.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: INSAT satellites are in geostationary orbit for continuous coverage of one area. Kalpana-1 (originally METSAT) was launched by PSLV in 2002 and renamed after Kalpana Chawla.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Astrosat was launched by GSLV.
2. XPoSat is India's first Earth observation satellite.
3. Astrosat is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Astrosat was launched by PSLV in September 2015 and observes in the ultraviolet, optical and X-ray bands. XPoSat (January 2024) is a polarimetry mission studying X-ray emission from cosmic sources.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. SpaDeX was launched by GSLV.
2. SpaDeX demonstrated the docking of two small satellites in orbit.
3. India became the fourth country to demonstrate space docking technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: SpaDeX flew on PSLV-C60 with two satellites, a chaser and a target, which docked in January 2025. Only the United States, Russia and China had done this before.
questions.h: Docking club: US, Russia, China, then India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India demonstrated an anti-satellite capability in 2019 under Mission Shakti.
2. The target of the Mission Shakti test was a satellite in the geostationary orbit.
3. India became the fourth country to have demonstrated such a capability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The interceptor hit a satellite in low Earth orbit at roughly 300 km. The other three countries are the US, Russia and China. A lower test altitude was chosen to limit the debris.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites
questions.h: ASAT club: US, Russia, China, India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station was established in 1963.
2. Thumba was chosen because it lies close to the Earth's magnetic equator.
3. The Satish Dhawan Space Centre is located in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, was ideal for upper-atmosphere studies as it is on the magnetic equator. The Satish Dhawan Space Centre is on Sriharikota island in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. SSLV : Designed to launch small satellites of up to about 500 kg to low Earth orbit
2. LVM3 : The launcher with ISRO's heaviest lift capacity
3. PSLV : Uses a cryogenic upper stage
4. GSLV Mk II : Uses a solid upper stage
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. PSLV has no cryogenic stage, and GSLV Mk II has an indigenous cryogenic upper stage as its third stage.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Cartosat : Earth imaging for cartography
2. NavIC : Remote sensing of oceans
3. GSAT-7 : Space-based astronomical observations
4. Astrosat : Weather forecasting
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 is correct. NavIC is a navigation system, GSAT-7 is a military communication satellite for the Navy and Astrosat is a space observatory.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A satellite in low Earth orbit takes roughly 90 to 120 minutes to orbit the Earth.
2. A satellite in a lower circular orbit moves faster than one in a higher orbit.
3. A geostationary satellite moves in the same sense as the Earth's rotation, from west to east.
4. The orbital period of a satellite increases as its altitude increases.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Gravity is stronger closer in, so lower satellites must move faster, and the longer path at greater height gives a longer period. The geostationary satellite takes 24 hours.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chang'e-4 : China - landed on the far side of the Moon
2. Hayabusa2 : Japan - returned samples from the asteroid Ryugu
3. Artemis : NASA - programme to return humans to the Moon
4. Luna-25 : European Space Agency - lunar lander
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Pairs 1 to 3 are correct. Luna-25 was a Russian lunar lander that crashed in August 2023, days before Chandrayaan-3 landed.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Aryabhata : Launched in 1975 by an Indian SLV-3
2. Bhaskara-I : Experimental Earth observation satellite
3. Rohini RS-1 : Launched by SLV-3 in 1980
4. APPLE : Launched by PSLV
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Aryabhata was launched from the Soviet Union in 1975, and APPLE, India's first experimental communication satellite, was launched by Europe's Ariane in 1981.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Geostationary satellites orbit above the Earth's poles.
2. India's first satellite Aryabhata was launched in 1980.
3. ISRO is headquartered in Hyderabad.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Geostationary satellites orbit above the equator, Aryabhata was launched in 1975 and ISRO's headquarters is in Bengaluru.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Communication satellites are generally placed in geostationary orbit.
Statement-II: A satellite in geostationary orbit remains fixed relative to a point on the ground, so a ground antenna need not track it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The fixed position allows continuous contact with a stationary dish, which is the main reason for choosing this orbit for TV and telecom.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Chandrayaan-3's lander touched down near the south polar region of the Moon.
Statement-II: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true but the launch vehicle has no bearing on the landing site, which was set by the mission design and the lander's guidance.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A rocket can operate in the vacuum of space.
Statement-II: A rocket moves forward by pushing against the atmospheric air.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Rockets rely on the reaction to expelled exhaust, not on air. That is why they work in space, where there is no air.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A geostationary satellite can provide continuous coverage of the entire Earth, including the polar regions.
Statement-II: A geostationary satellite orbits in the equatorial plane at about 35,786 km above the Earth.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because it sits over the equator, a geostationary satellite covers only a portion of the globe and has poor coverage at high latitudes. Polar regions are better served by polar orbiting satellites.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Remote sensing satellites used for resource monitoring are generally placed in Sun-synchronous polar orbits.
Statement-II: In such an orbit, the satellite passes over a place at the same local solar time, so images taken on different dates have comparable illumination.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Consistent lighting makes it easy to compare images over time to track changes in crops, forests or water bodies.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (ISRO centre)
A. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
B. U R Rao Satellite Centre
C. Space Applications Centre
D. National Remote Sensing Centre
List-II (Location)
1. Hyderabad
2. Ahmedabad
3. Bengaluru
4. Thiruvananthapuram
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: VSSC (launch vehicles) is in Thiruvananthapuram, URSC (satellites) in Bengaluru, SAC (payloads and applications) in Ahmedabad and NRSC (remote sensing data) in Hyderabad.
questions.h: V-Vehicles in Thiruvananthapuram; U-satellites in Bengaluru.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Mission)
A. Mangalyaan
B. Astrosat
C. Aditya-L1
D. XPoSat
List-II (Feature)
1. Study of the Sun from the Sun-Earth L1 point
2. Orbiter around Mars
3. Multi-wavelength space observatory
4. X-ray polarimetry
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Mangalyaan is the Mars Orbiter Mission, Astrosat is an astronomy observatory, Aditya-L1 studies the Sun from L1, and XPoSat is India's X-ray polarimetry mission.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Orbit)
A. Geostationary orbit
B. Low Earth orbit
C. Sun-synchronous orbit
D. Medium Earth orbit
List-II (Typical use)
1. International Space Station
2. Navigation constellations such as GPS
3. INSAT communication satellites
4. Earth-observation satellites with constant illumination
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: INSATs sit at 35,786 km, the ISS is at about 400 km, polar Sun-synchronous orbits suit imaging, and GPS satellites orbit at about 20,000 km in medium Earth orbit.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Launch vehicle)
A. SLV-3
B. ASLV
C. PSLV
D. GSLV
List-II (Feature)
1. Workhorse for polar and Sun-synchronous orbits
2. Launched Rohini RS-1 in 1980
3. Designed for geosynchronous transfer orbit
4. Augmented with strap-on boosters
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: SLV-3 was India's first launcher, ASLV added strap-on boosters, PSLV became the workhorse, and GSLV was built to reach geosynchronous transfer orbit.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Private space company)
A. Skyroot Aerospace
B. Agnikul Cosmos
C. Pixxel
D. Digantara
List-II (Area of work)
1. Hyperspectral imaging satellites
2. Space situational awareness
3. Vikram series of launch vehicles
4. Agnibaan launch vehicle with a 3D-printed engine
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Skyroot built Vikram-S, Agnikul built the Agnibaan, Pixxel builds hyperspectral satellites and Digantara tracks objects in orbit.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Indian satellites in the chronological order of their launch:
1. Aryabhata
2. Rohini RS-1
3. Bhaskara-I
4. APPLE
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: Aryabhata (1975), Bhaskara-I (1979), Rohini RS-1 (1980, India's first on its own launcher SLV-3) and APPLE (1981).

questions.q:
Arrange the following Indian missions in the chronological order of their launch:
1. Aditya-L1
2. Chandrayaan-2
3. Astrosat
4. Mangalyaan
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: Mangalyaan (2013), Astrosat (2015), Chandrayaan-2 (2019) and Aditya-L1 (September 2023).

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the increasing order of their typical altitude above the Earth:
1. International Space Station
2. GPS satellites
3. Geostationary satellites
4. Sun-synchronous Earth-observation satellites
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: The ISS is at about 400 km, Sun-synchronous satellites at roughly 500 to 800 km, GPS at about 20,000 km and geostationary satellites at 35,786 km.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched from
o: the Soviet Union, on a Soviet launch vehicle
Kourou in French Guiana, on Ariane
questions.e: Aryabhata went up in April 1975 from Kapustin Yar. India put a satellite in orbit with its own launcher only in 1980 with Rohini on SLV-3.

questions.q: The propellants used in a cryogenic upper stage are
questions.e: Both are gases liquefied at very low temperatures; they give high thrust for each kilogram of propellant. UDMH and N2O4 power Vikas engines, kerosene with LOX is semi-cryogenic, and HTPB-based fuel is solid propellant.

questions.q: The first rocket launched from Thumba, in November 1963, was a
questions.e: Sounding rockets for studying the upper atmosphere were the beginning of the Indian space programme, and the first was an American-built Nike-Apache. ISRO's own Rohini sounding rockets and SLV-3 followed later.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT an independent satellite navigation constellation?
questions.e: GAGAN is a satellite-based augmentation system developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India that improves the accuracy of GPS signals for aviation. NavIC, Galileo and GLONASS are their own constellations.

questions.q: The Aditya-L1 spacecraft is positioned at the Sun-Earth L1 point, which is about
questions.e: L1 lies about 1% of the way along the Earth-Sun line (roughly 1.5 million km). The Moon's distance is about 384,000 km and the Sun's is about 150 million km.

questions.q: Chandrayaan-1 is credited with
o: the first soft landing near the lunar south pole
discovering a global magnetic field on the Moon
bringing back lunar soil samples to the Earth
detecting water molecules and hydroxyl on the lunar surface
questions.e: Its NASA-provided Moon Mineralogy Mapper detected signatures of water and hydroxyl, and the ISRO Moon Impact Probe was released to hit the surface. The soft landing came 15 years later with Chandrayaan-3.

questions.q: The Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) is designed to launch satellites of up to about 500 kg into
questions.e: SSLV is a three-stage solid vehicle with a liquid velocity trimming module, aimed at the on-demand market for small satellites in low Earth orbit.

questions.q: A geosynchronous satellite differs from a geostationary satellite in that the geosynchronous satellite
o: has an orbital period of 12 hours
orbits at an altitude of about 800 km
revolves in a direction opposite to the Earth's rotation
may have an inclined orbit and so trace a figure-of-eight path in the sky
questions.e: Both have a period equal to the Earth's rotation period (24 hours). Only the geostationary satellite has zero inclination and a circular orbit over the equator, so it appears fixed; NavIC's four inclined satellites are geosynchronous.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q: Which one of the following is an active remote sensing technique?
o: Optical imaging in the visible band using sunlight
questions.e: LiDAR emits laser pulses and measures the returned signal; the other options measure reflected sunlight or the Earth's own emitted radiation, so they are passive.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q: To determine the three-dimensional position of a receiver and correct its clock error, a satellite navigation receiver needs signals from at least
questions.e: Latitude, longitude and altitude need three range measurements, and the receiver's clock error adds a fourth unknown, so four satellites are needed.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q: The minimum velocity needed by an object at the Earth's surface to escape the Earth's gravitational pull is about
questions.e: 7.9 km/s is the circular orbital speed near the surface; escape velocity is greater by a factor of the square root of two (about 11.2 km/s). That is why a satellite stays bound but a deep-space probe must exceed it.
questions.s: Standard S&T reference: orbits and satellites

questions.q: Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian to travel to space, flew in 1984 aboard
questions.e: He flew to the Salyut-7 space station under an Indo-Soviet programme. Kalpana Chawla, an Indian-born astronaut, flew on the Space Shuttle Columbia.
